# opencode-memorysync

Automatic long-term memory for [OpenCode](https://opencode.ai), powered by
[MemorySync](https://memorysync.io). One line in your config and every session
starts already briefed on you and your project — recalled context is injected
into the system prompt, the durable facts in your messages are captured as you
send them, and the MemorySync MCP servers and slash commands are registered
for you.

## Install

Add one line to `~/.config/opencode/opencode.json` (or a project's
`.opencode.json`); OpenCode installs the plugin from npm on next start:

```json
{ "plugin": ["opencode-memorysync"] }
```

Then set your API key (get one at [app.memorysync.io](https://app.memorysync.io)):

```bash
# macOS/Linux
export MEMORYSYNC_API_KEY=ms_...
# Windows
setx MEMORYSYNC_API_KEY ms_...
```

Without a key, the MemorySync MCP server falls back to OAuth — OpenCode signs
you in on first tool use (`opencode mcp auth`).

## What runs when

| Moment | What happens |
| --- | --- |
| First LLM call of a session | Your profile and this project's context are recalled once and injected into the system prompt; every later call in the session replays the identical block from a bounded cache. |
| You send a message | The text is sent to MemorySync, which extracts the durable facts in it and stores only those, tagged with the `opencode::<project>` session scope; the message text itself is not stored. A content-hash seed lets the server recognise a replayed message so it is not extracted twice, and a failed send can be retried by a later event. Slash-command template expansions are recognised and skipped. |
| The reply completes | Nothing is sent: assistant replies are not stored as memories. |
| Session compaction | Memory context is re-supplied to what survives the compact. |
| Any failure — no key, network down, monthly quota exhausted | Silent skip. Every hook is wrapped: a thrown hook would break your OpenCode session, so none can throw. |

## What gets registered

- **MCP servers** — `memorysync` (the full memory tool set; API-key auth when
  `MEMORYSYNC_API_KEY` is set, OAuth otherwise) and `memorysync-docs`
  (zero-auth documentation search).
- **Slash commands** — `/memorysync-recall <query>`, `/memorysync-remember
  <fact>`, `/memorysync-status`.

Registration is non-destructive: MCP or command entries you configured
yourself are never overwritten.

## Configuration

| Variable | Effect |
| --- | --- |
| `MEMORYSYNC_API_KEY` | Authenticates capture, recall and the MCP server. |
| `MEMORYSYNC_USER_ID` | Memory identity (default: OS username). |
| `MEMORYSYNC_PROJECT` | Project scope override (default: git remote, worktree-aware). |
| `MEMORYSYNC_BASE_URL` | Point at a different MemorySync deployment. |
| `MEMORYSYNC_PROMPT_RECALL=off` | Disable system-prompt injection; capture and tools keep working. |
| `MEMORYSYNC_DISABLE=1` | Switch the plugin off without uninstalling. |
